titel: The protest of the Bohemian lords
autor: The barons, lords, knights and squires of Bohemia and Moravia, assembled at Prague
quelle: F. Palacký (ed.), Documenta Mag. Joannis Hus vitam, doctrinam, causam in Constantiensi concilio actam ... illustrantia (Prague: Tempsky, 1869), no. 85, pp. 580–584. Internet Archive, documentamagjoa00palagoog. Public domain.
hinweis: Palacký prints the letter from several manuscripts, with the names of all who sealed its eight copies; the names are not carried here. Read against the page images; abbreviated titles are written out. Three excerpts covering most of the letter; cuts are marked [...]. The English is this site's working translation (CC0).

sections.titel: The lords' letter to the council, 2 September 1415
sections.blurb: Gathered in Prague, the lords of Bohemia and Moravia send the council a letter under 452 seals: Hus was a good, just and catholic man, condemned unheard; whoever calls Bohemia heretical lies on his own head, the king excepted; and they will defend the preachers of the law of Christ even to the shedding of blood.

units.orig: Reverendissimis in Christo patribus et dominis, dominis cardinalibus, patriarchis, primatibus, archiepiscopis, episcopis, ambasiatoribus, doctoribus et magistris, ac toti concilio Constantiensi: nos Čenko de Wesele, alias de Wartenberg, supremus burgravius Pragensis, Lacko de Krawař, capitaneus marchionatus Moraviae, Bočko senior de Kunstat, alias de Podiebrad, [...] magnates, barones, proceres et nobiles christianissimi regni Bohemiae et praeclarissimi marchionatus Moraviae: affectum omnis boni et observantiam Jesu Christi domini nostri mandatorum. Sane, quia jure naturali et divino cuilibet jubetur alii facere, quod sibi vult fieri, et prohibetur alii inferre, quod sibi nolit fieri, [...] nos itaque praefatae legi divinae et dilectioni proximi, quantum possumus, deo auctore intendentes, pro carissimo proximo nostro, bonae memoriae venerando magistro Joanne Hus, sacrae theologiae baccalaureo formato, praedicatore evangelico, quem nuper in concilio Constantiensi, nescimus quo spiritu ducti, non confessum, nec legitime ut decebat convictum, nullisque contra eum deductis et ostensis erroribus et haeresibus, sed ad sinistras falsas et importunas suorum et regni nostri et marchionatus Moraviae capitalium inimicorum et proditorum accusationes, delationes et instigationes, tamquam haereticum pertinacem condemnastis et condemnatum dira et turpissima morte affecistis, in nostri regni Bohemiae christianissimi et marchionatus Moraviae clarissimi ac omnium nostrum perpetuam infamiam et notam, — quemadmodum serenissimo principi et domino D. Sigismundo Romanorum et Hungariae &c. regi, heredi et domino nostro successuro, scripta nostra ad Constantiam transmisimus, quae etiam in congregationibus vestris lecta sunt et publicata, et quae hic habere volumus pro insertis, (et ea, ut refertur, in nostrum dedecus et contemptum, ignis voragini tradidistis) — ita et nunc Paternitatibus Vestris pro dicto M. Joanne Hus literas nostras patentes praesentibus duximus destinandas, publice corde et ore confitentes et protestantes, quod ipse M. Joannes Hus fuit vir utique bonus, justus et catholicus, a multis annis in regno nostro vita, moribus et fama laudabiliter conversatus et comprobatus; legem etiam evangelicam et sanctorum prophetarum, novi et veteris testamenti libros, juxta expositionem sanctorum doctorum ab ecclesia approbatorum, nos et subditos nostros catholice docuit, praedicavit et in scriptis multa reliquit, omnes errores et haereses constantissime detestando, [...] ita quod numquam audivimus, nec intelligere potuimus, etiam omni diligentia apposita, quod praefatus M. Joannes Hus quenquam errorem vel haeresim in suis sermonibus docuisset, praedicasset vel quovis modo asseruisset, seu nos vel nostros subditos verbo vel facto quoquomodo scandalisasset: quinimo pie et mansuete in Christo vivens, omnes ad servandam legem evangelicam et sanctorum patrum instituta, pro aedificatione sanctae matris ecclesiae et salute proximorum, quantum potuit, verbo et opere diligentissime hortabatur.
units.en: To the most reverend fathers and lords in Christ, the lord cardinals, patriarchs, primates, archbishops, bishops, ambassadors, doctors and masters, and to the whole council of Constance: we, Čeněk of Veselí, also called of Wartenberg, supreme burgrave of Prague, Lacek of Kravaře, captain of the margraviate of Moravia, Boček the elder of Kunštát, also called of Poděbrady, [...] magnates, barons, lords and nobles of the most Christian kingdom of Bohemia and the most illustrious margraviate of Moravia: the will to every good and the keeping of the commandments of Jesus Christ our Lord. Since by natural and divine law everyone is commanded to do to another what he wishes done to himself, and forbidden to inflict on another what he would not have done to himself, [...] we, attending as far as we can, with God's help, to that divine law and to the love of our neighbour, on behalf of our dearest neighbour, the venerable Master Jan Hus of good memory, formed bachelor of sacred theology, preacher of the gospel, whom lately in the council of Constance, led by we know not what spirit, you condemned as an obstinate heretic, though he had not confessed, nor been lawfully convicted as was fitting, and no errors or heresies had been brought forward and shown against him, but at the malicious, false and importunate accusations, denunciations and instigations of his and our kingdom's and the margraviate of Moravia's mortal enemies and traitors; and, condemned, you put him to a dreadful and most shameful death, to the perpetual disgrace and stain of our most Christian kingdom of Bohemia and most illustrious margraviate of Moravia and of us all (as we sent our writings to Constance to the most serene prince and lord, the lord Sigismund, king of the Romans and of Hungary etc., our heir and lord to come, which were also read and made public in your congregations, and which we wish to be held as inserted here; and these, it is reported, you gave to the jaws of the fire, to our dishonour and contempt): so now too we have resolved to send to Your Paternities our letters patent on behalf of the said Master Jan Hus, publicly confessing and protesting with heart and mouth that this Master Jan Hus was a man good, just and catholic in every way, who for many years lived in our kingdom in praiseworthy conduct, character and repute, and was proved; who taught us and our subjects in a catholic way the law of the gospel and the books of the holy prophets, of the New and Old Testament, according to the exposition of the holy doctors approved by the Church, preached it and left much in writing, most steadfastly detesting all errors and heresies [...]; so that we never heard, nor could learn, even with all diligence, that the said Master Jan Hus taught, preached or in any way asserted any error or heresy in his sermons, or gave offence by word or deed in any way to us or our subjects: on the contrary, living piously and gently in Christ, he exhorted all most diligently, as far as he could, by word and deed, to keep the law of the gospel and the ordinances of the holy fathers, for the building up of holy mother Church and the salvation of their neighbours.
units.note: The opening names the leading barons of Bohemia and Moravia (cut here), headed by Čeněk of Wartenberg, the highest officer of the kingdom, and Lacek of Kravaře, captain of Moravia. 'Not confessed, not lawfully convicted': the lords answer the sentence on its own legal ground (Decr. Sentence [1], [2]). Their earlier letters to Sigismund, among them the Czech petition of 12 May (Council Lords [1], [2]), had been read at Constance; the lords had heard that the council burned them. The council's own letter of 26 July to the barons of Bohemia had said that Hus was heard many times, 'confessed' absurd beliefs and was 'convicted' of open heresy (Council Letter [1]); the lords answer it word for word: not confessed, not convicted. Like the defence of the Kutná Hora decree (KH Defence [2]), the letter opens with the golden rule.

units.orig: Nec praemissa omnia in confusionem nostram et regni ac marchionatus praefatorum perpetrata vobis suffecerunt: quin potius honorandum M. Hieronymum de Praga, virum certissime lacteo eloquentiae fonte manantem, septem artium liberalium magistrum et philosophum utique illustrem, non visum, non auditum, non confessum nec convictum, sed ad solam suorum et nostrorum proditorum sinistram traditionem, sine omni misericordia comprehensum incarcerastis et trucidastis, et jam forte, sicut et M. Joannem Hus, crudelissima morte interemistis. Praeterea ad nostram, quod nimis dolenter referimus, pervenit audientiam et ex scriptis vestris collegimus evidenter, quomodo quidam detractores, deo et hominibus odibiles, ac nostri regni Bohemiae et marchionatus Moraviae aemuli et proditores, coram vobis et concilio vestro nos et regnum ac marchionatum praedictos gravissime et nequissime detulerunt, asserentes, licet false, mendose et proditorie, quod in praefatis regno Bohemiae et marchionatu Moraviae diversi errores et haereses pullularunt [...]. Ut autem, juxta sententiam apostoli, provideamus bona non solum coram deo, sed etiam coram hominibus, et ne propter negligentiam celeberrimae famae praedictorum regni et marchionatus nostrorum crudeles erga proximos nostros reperiamur: ideo [...] tenore praesentium Vestris Paternitatibus et universis Christi fidelibus innotescimus et insinuamus, corde et ore publice profitentes: quod quicunque hominum cujuscunque status, praeeminentiae vel dignitatis, conditionis, gradus vel religionis exstiterit, qui dixit vel asseruit, dicit vel asserit, quod in praefatis regno Bohemiae et marchionatu Moraviae errores et haereses pullulassent, ac nos et alios Christi fideles ipsorum ut praemittitur infecissent, — sola persona serenissimi principis et domini D. Sigismundi Romanorum &c. regis, heredis ac domini nostri successuri semota, quem in praemissis credimus et speramus innoxium, — omnis et quilibet talis, ut praefertur, recte mentitur in caput suum, tamquam nequam pessimus traditor et proditor praedictorum regni et marchionatus ac noster perfidissimus, et solus utique haereticus perniciosissimus, omnisque malitiae et nequitiae imo et diaboli filius, qui mendax est et pater ejus.
units.en: Nor did all this, done to the confusion of us and of the said kingdom and margraviate, suffice you: rather, the honourable Master Jerome of Prague, a man most surely flowing from a milky fountain of eloquence, master of the seven liberal arts and a truly illustrious philosopher, not seen, not heard, not confessed nor convicted, but on the sole malicious betrayal of his and our traitors, you seized without any mercy, imprisoned and tormented, and perhaps have already put to a most cruel death, as you did Master Jan Hus. Moreover it has come to our hearing, as we report with great sorrow, and we have gathered plainly from your own writings, how certain slanderers, hateful to God and men, enemies and traitors of our kingdom of Bohemia and margraviate of Moravia, have denounced us and the said kingdom and margraviate before you and your council most gravely and wickedly, asserting, though falsely, lyingly and treacherously, that various errors and heresies have sprung up in the said kingdom of Bohemia and margraviate of Moravia [...]. But so that, in the apostle's words, we may provide things good not only before God but also before men, and may not be found cruel towards our neighbours by neglecting the most celebrated good name of our said kingdom and margraviate: therefore [...] by these presents we make known and declare to Your Paternities and to all Christ's faithful, publicly professing with heart and mouth, that whoever of men, of whatever estate, pre-eminence or dignity, condition, rank or religious order, has said or asserted, or says or asserts, that errors and heresies have sprung up in the said kingdom of Bohemia and margraviate of Moravia and have infected us and other faithful of Christ, as said above (setting apart only the person of the most serene prince and lord, the lord Sigismund, king of the Romans etc., our heir and lord to come, whom we believe and hope to be innocent in these things), each and every such person, as said, lies rightly on his own head, as a worthless, most wicked betrayer and traitor of the said kingdom and margraviate and most faithless to us, and is himself the most pernicious heretic, and a son of all malice and wickedness, indeed of the devil, who is a liar and the father of it.
units.note: Jerome of Prague, Hus's friend, had been arrested on his way home from Constance in April 1415 and was still in prison; he was burned on 30 May 1416. The lords did not know whether he was alive. The second paragraph turns the charge of heresy back on the accusers, in the formal language of a challenge. The one exception is pointed: Sigismund, whose safe conduct Hus had carried (Mlad. Journey [1]), is named their heir and lord to come and 'believed and hoped' innocent. The kingdom would be his on Wenceslas's death, and the lords left him a way back. The cut passage recalls Bohemia's loyalty to the Roman Church through the schism.

units.orig: Nihilominus tamen praemissas injurias domino, cujus est vindicta et qui abundanter retribuet facientibus superbiam, nunc committentes, apud futurum apostolicum, quem dominus deus suae sanctae ecclesiae praefecerit unicum et indubitatum pastorem, illas amplius et latius prosequemur; cui deo volente tamquam fideles filii, in his quae sunt licita et honesta, rationi et legi divinae consona, reverentiam et obedientiam debitam exhibentes, petemus et postulabimus in et super praemissis omnibus et singulis, juxta legem domini nostri Jesu Christi et sanctorum patrum instituta, nobis et praefatis regno et marchionatui provideri de remedio opportuno. Praemissis tamen non obstantibus, legem domini nostri Jesu Christi ipsiusque devotos et humiles ac constantes praedicatores usque effusionem sanguinis, omni timore et statutis humanis in contrarium editis posttergatis, defendere volumus et tueri. Datum Pragae anno domini MCCCCXV°, die secunda mensis Septembris, in pleno concilio magnatum, baronum, procerum et nobilium regni Bohemiae et marchionatus Moraviae, nostrorum sub appensione sigillorum.
units.en: Nevertheless, committing these wrongs now to the Lord, whose is vengeance and who will repay abundantly those who act in pride, we will pursue them further and more widely before the future apostolic lord whom the Lord God shall set over his holy Church as its one and undoubted shepherd; to whom, God willing, as faithful sons, showing due reverence and obedience in what is lawful and honest and in keeping with reason and the divine law, we will ask and demand that a fitting remedy be provided for us and for the said kingdom and margraviate in and concerning all and each of the above, according to the law of our Lord Jesus Christ and the ordinances of the holy fathers. All this notwithstanding, we will defend and protect the law of our Lord Jesus Christ and its devout, humble and steadfast preachers even to the shedding of blood, putting behind us all fear and all human statutes issued to the contrary. Given at Prague in the year of the Lord 1415, on the second day of the month of September, in the full assembly of the magnates, barons, lords and nobles of the kingdom of Bohemia and the margraviate of Moravia, with our seals hung below.
units.note: In September 1415 there was no pope: John XXIII had been deposed in May, Gregory XII had resigned in July, and Benedict XIII was holding out in Aragon. The lords appeal past the council to a pope not yet elected, and promise him obedience only 'in what is lawful and in keeping with the divine law', the same condition Hus had set (De eccl. [5]). The last sentence is the one that mattered: the defence of 'the preachers of the law of Christ' 'even to the shedding of blood' against 'human statutes'. Palacký records that eight letters of this text went to the council, with 35, 100, 102 and 84 seals from Bohemia and 24, 26, 27 and 54 from Moravia, 452 in all; the original of the second, with its hundred seals, was then, as now, in the library of the University of Edinburgh. Three days later, on 5 September, the lords bound themselves in a league to protect free preaching on their estates.
